Definition: from G3844 and a derivative of G3691; to sharpen alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--easily provoke, stir.
BiblicalUsage: Paroxyno means to sharpen alongside, to provoke, to stir up. It appears twice: in Acts 17:16 Paul's spirit is stirred within him when he sees Athens wholly given to idolatry, and in 1 Corinthians 13:5 love is not easily provoked. The Greek text spells this word paroxynomai, the middle voice of the same verb; the site's spelling is the same verb under its Strong's form.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there is a stirring that is holy and a stirring that is not, and the difference is the cause: Paul stirred by idols, and love refusing to be stirred by offence.
